subject: general
question: In ∆ABC if ∠A = 70º and ∠B = 70º, find the measure of exterior angle A.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **exterior angle** at any vertex of a triangle and the corresponding **interior angle** are **supplementary**.

Exterior Angle A = 180° − Interior Angle A

⇒ Exterior Angle A = 180° − 70° = 110°

**∴ The correct answer is 110°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** In **ΔABC**, interior **∠A = 70°** and interior **∠B = 70°**.

**Formula Used:** 1. Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°. 2. Exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two **opposite interior angles**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8ee5a98b988968a852bfabcdd77c587643168d29725e17175dcf1f26ef795210.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, find the third interior angle **∠C**:

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 70° + 70° + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 140° + ∠C = 180° ⇒ ∠C = 40°

⇒ **Exterior angle A** is the sum of opposite interior angles **∠B** and **∠C**.

⇒ Exterior ∠A = ∠B + ∠C

⇒ Exterior ∠A = 70° + 40°

⇒ Exterior ∠A = 110°

**∴ The correct answer is 110°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of its two opposite non-adjacent interior angles.

Linear Pair Postulate

The sum of an interior angle and its corresponding exterior angle at a vertex is always 180° because they form a linear pair.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of all three exterior angles (one at each vertex) of any triangle is always 360°.</p
